commands.review_summary:
The PR makes prompt-build hook suppression implicit via an AsyncLocalStorage reentrancy guard around embedded-attempt hook resolution and adds helper/active-memory tests for the active-memory recall sub-run.

PR surface: Source +38, Tests +75. Total +113 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main source shows active-memory recall is a non-raw embedded run that re-enters prompt-build hooks, and a focused Node probe shows the PR's AsyncLocalStorage value persists into a timer created during dispatch.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can preserve the current design while fixing the async-scope leak and adding targeted regression coverage.

target.title: fix(active-memory): skip prompt-build hooks in the recall sub-run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The active-memory extension dispatches its per-turn recall sub-completion through `runEmbeddedAgent` without marking it as an internal run, so the full plugin `before_prompt_build` hook chain executes inside every recall sub-build. Every installed plugin pays that cost on every turn, and plugins that inject prompt material end up decorating a throwaway internal memory-search run: in live traces the recall sub-run's system prompt carried thousands of characters of other plugins' hook contributions (recall-policy and compacted-context sections) that have no business in a memory lookup. Memory plugins can also re-enter their own injection logic from inside the sub-build.

Passing `modelRun: true` / `promptMode: "none"` is not a viable fix: `isRawModelRun` also disables tool construction, the context engine, and the system prompt, which would break the recall sub-run itself (it depends on its configured memory-search tool).

## Fix

- Adds a narrow, additive `skipPromptBuildHooks` run param that skips exactly the prompt-build hook resolution (queued injections, `agent_turn_prepare`, heartbeat contribution, `before_prompt_build`, legacy `before_agent_start`) and nothing else. Tool construction, the context engine, and the system prompt are untouched. Threaded params to run to attempt via a pure helper, `shouldSkipPromptBuildHooks`.
- The active-memory recall dispatch passes `skipPromptBuildHooks: true`.
- The param is not exposed on the gateway wire schema; it is reachable only by in-process callers. Every other internal sub-run caller already uses `modelRun: true`, so no other call site consumes these hooks mid-run.

## Evidence

- Live verification on a deployed build (2026-07-09, real traffic, request payloads inspected via tracing): before the change, every recall sub-run's system prompt measured 10,914 chars and included hook-contributed sections from an installed memory plugin ("Lossless Recall Policy", "Compacted Conversation Context") plus channel reaction guidance; after the change the same sub-runs measure 5,040 chars with those sections gone, consistent across two agents and multiple turns. Recall behavior itself is unchanged: the sub-run still receives its own instructions, prompt append, and memory-search tool, completes with normal latency, and returns results.
- Focused tests: three new unit tests for the helper, plus a new active-memory test asserting the recall dispatch passes the flag AND that the recall prompt (instructions, prompt append, query, all built locally by the extension) still reaches the sub-run. Red/green verified by reverting just the invoker line (the new test fails with `expected undefined to be true`) and restoring. Touched suites: 18/18, 158/158, 116/116 passing.

## Notes

- The recall prompt's own content is built by the extension and is not a `before_prompt_build` product; the new test pins that down explicitly so this cannot silently starve recall.
